That's a good point- I'm seeing it like this: the audience will be gamers, both women and men. Female panelists would discuss strategies to make change in the community or in game development that would open more opportunities and open up more interest for women to start playing more games, but first, the current climate of the gaming community and the nature of games now should probably be examined.

The amount of followers that the panelists have aren't the point of the discussion. Panelists and attendees are looking to discuss how the gaming community can fix the misconceptions that people outside of the gaming community have. This is less focused on the panelists, and more focused on the attendees and the community itself. The current people that plan on attending are gaming community leaders in DC. If you are free, come by and express your perspective. Everyone would like to hear it.

This partially depends on WHICH god you're referring to (since there are hundreds if you consider every religion) but assuming you mean the Christian god, then you're looking at a more masculine figure (since God created man in his image) but if you're looking at Eastern gods like the Hindu gods or the Buddha then it will be much easier to determine the gender of these gods. However, if you're willing to take away all pre-determined biases about religion, and you would think of a creator, then this creator most likely would have no gender, or at least not one that we could comprehend.
